title: An Activatable NIR Yb4Zn2 Cluster for the Detection of Quercetin: Analysis of Host–Guest Interaction and Sensing Mechanism

material_class.structural_family: centrosymmetric rod-like/dumbbell Yb4Zn2 Schiff-base acetate cluster

synthesis.procedure: Yb(OAc)3·4H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.084 g), Zn(OAc)2·2H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.044 g), and H2L (0.20 mmol, 0.077 g) were dissolved in 9 mL EtOH and 3 mL MeOH at room temperature, and triethylamine in MeOH (1.0 mol/L, 1 mL) was added. The solution was stirred and heated under reflux for 30 min, cooled, and filtered. Diethyl ether was allowed to diffuse slowly into the filtrate at room temperature, giving pale red-yellow crystals after two weeks. The crystals were filtered, washed with EtOH (3 × 5 mL), and dried in air for two weeks.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature for dissolution and crystallization; reflux for 30 min
synthesis.time: reflux 30 min; crystallization two weeks; air drying two weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux followed by diethyl-ether vapor diffusion into the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled and filtered; slow diethyl-ether diffusion at room temperature for two weeks; crystals washed with EtOH (3 × 5 mL) and dried in air

properties.summary: Cluster 1 shows ligand-sensitized NIR Yb(III) emission at 980 nm (2F5/2 → 2F7/2) upon 360 nm excitation in CH3CN. Excitation at 460 nm does not produce Yb emission until quercetin is added; the host–guest interaction activates NIR fluorescence, enabling selective detection of quercetin with a 5 s response and a 0.75 μM detection limit (0–50 μM range).
